# win32 under --simulate, with no C toolchain and no Wine: the interpreter
# runs the target's overrides -- a canvas's text among them, which no other
# target's override draws through win32's context -- and makes, fills and
# connects each node through the #[gen.protocol] functions win32.sngl
# declares, every runtime call a stubbed #[cnative]. A string the runtime is
# handed is a `c.utf16` the turn's arena holds, so the tracker has none to
# follow, and the run ends with nothing held.

env PATH=

sngl test --simulate win32 app.sngl
stdout '^ok   1 tests, 0 failures$'
! stdout 'leak'

-- app.sngl --
import ui "sngl:ui"
import draw "sngl:ui/draw"
import test "sngl:test"

output {
    c {
        win32
    }
}

component page ui.node {
    var n = 0

    ui.vbox {
        ui.text("{n}")
        ui.link(text="site", href="https://example.com")
        draw.canvas(width=60px, height=20px) {
            draw.canvasText(x=0.0, y=16.0, content="n {n}", style=draw.Style{fill=#000000, fontFamily="serif"})
        }
        ui.button #more(text="more", @click {
            n = n + 1
        })
    }
}

func testCounts(t test.Test, c page) {
    c.n = 2
    c.more.click()
    t.assert(c.n == 3)
}

ui.window(title="t") {
    page
}
